Indian Standard TEXTILES -- HIGH DENSITY POLYETHYLENE (HDPE)/POLYPROPYLENE (PP) WOVEN SACK FOR SAND -- SPECIFICATION (First Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard specifies requirements for high density polyethylene (HDPE)/polypropy lene(PP) woven sacks used for filling sand. 2 REFERENCES The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated in Annex A. 3 MANUFACTURE 3.1 Raw Material The tape shall be manufactured from virgin high density polyethylene(HDPE)/polypropylene (PP) granules (see IS 6192 and IS 11 197). 3.2 Fabric The fabric used in the manufacture of HDPE/PP woven sacks shall be woven from HDPE/PP tapes having minimum linear density of 750 denier and conforming to 1S 6192 or IS 11197. The tapes shall be stabilized against deterioration due to sunlight by using any ultraviolet inhibiting system such as pigmentation by mixing 2 to 2.5 percent carbon black in the granules or if required by the purchaser, shall be manufactured from ultra-violet stabilized grade of HDPE/PP granules. The width of tape used for making fabric shall be minimum 2.5 mm. 3.3 Tying Cord 3-strand hawser-laid polypropylene 4 mm nominal diameter conforming be used. 3.4 Sack 3.4.1 Seam Sacks are manufactured from tubular woven fabric, 1 rope of having to IS 5175 shall the sacks shall be closed at the bottom by stitching with two rows of lock or chain type stitches separated from each other by minimum 4 mm and the outer row of stitches shall be minimum 5 mm from the edge of the sack. The stitching shall be done with fold over seam to a depth of 25 mm so that stitches pass through minimum 6 layers of fabric. Mouth of the sack shall form a channel of 30 mm width for passage of the tying cord, with turn-in of 10 mm, secured with lock stitch or chain stitch. The length of tying cord shall not be less than 1 m. The number of stitches per dm shall be 12 q 2. The stitching shall be uniform without any loose thread or knot. All loose threads shall be properly secured. 3.4.1.1 The material used for stitching shall be HDPE/ PP tape or any other thread suitable for the purposes, compatible to the product being packed in the sack. The HDPE/PP tape used for stitching shall have at least 20 percent higher denier than that used for making the sack. 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 The sacks shall conform specified in Table 1. 4.2 UV Resistance In case of PP woven fabric of sack made out of UV stabilized material shall have at least 50 percent of the original breaking strength when tested after the same has been exposed to UV radiation and weathering as per the method given in Annex B. 4.3 Mass of Bale The mass of bale of sacks (excluding packing materials) shall be within + 3 percent of the mass calculated by multiplying the number of sacks with the mass specified in Table 1. 5 PRINTING AND PACKAGING to the requirements

5.1 Printing on Sacks The sacks shall be printed with identification mark of sack manufacturer along with the information as

5.2 Packing

The sacks shall be packed to form a bale using a layer of HDPE/PP woven fabric and suitably secured. The bale shall contain 500 sacks and multiple thereof. 5.3 The bales shall be marked information: a) b) c) d) e) f) with the following

Prior to test, the specimens shall be conditioned to moisture equilibrium from dry side in the standard atmosphere of 65 * 2 percent relative humidity and 27+ 2�C temperature as laid down in 1S 6359. 7 SAMPLING CONFORMITY 7.1 Lot All the sacks of the same construction in a consignment shall be grouped together to constitute a lot. 7.2 The conformity of the lot to the requirements of the standard shall be determined on the basis of the test carried out on the samples selected from it. 7.3 The number of samples to be selected depends on the size of the lot and the number of bales to be sampled shall be in accordance with CO11 and COI2 of Table 2. The number of sacks to be selected from the bales sampled shall be in accordance with COI3 of Table 2 for visual inspections, dimensions, ends, picks and mass requirements and shall be in accordance with co] 4 of Table 2 for breaking strength of fabric before and after exposing to UV radiation, breaking strength of seam and percent elongation at break requirements. 2 AND CRITERIA FOR

Name of the manufacturer, Type and size of sacks, Gross mass, Net mass, Month and year of manufacture, Any other information Marking sacks may also be and required by the buyer.

ANNEX B (Clause 4.2)
UV RESISTANCE
B- I TO cictermine the effect of UV radiation and weathering on the breaking strength of PP woven fabric, the same shall be exposed as follows.

TEST

B-3 TEST PROCEDURE Specimens are alternately exposed to ultra-violet light alone and to condensation repeatedly. Condensation is produced by exposing the test surface to a heated, saturated mixture of air and water vapour, while the reverse side of the test specimen is exposed to the cooling influence of ambient room air.

B-2 TEST CONDITIONS The test shall be carried out with lamp. The duration of the test shall days). The test cycle shall be 8 h at rwiiation alternating with 4 hat 50+ fluorescent UV-B be 144 h (that is, 6 60 + 3�C with UV 3�C condensation.
